items.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: So we’d be studying like a Bach prelude or a Bach fugue and the harmonic structure of that

ctx.x: Well talking about memorizing tunes, do they help you out in school with suggestions, like here’s tunes you should know?

Well I haven’t really found that, no. But I haven’t really taken any — I took one jazz composition class at school, but I don’t have any jazz lessons. Like my lessons are classical, and all my harmony has been classical and ear training has been classical. So I find that I just apply that to jazz. So we’d be studying like a Bach prelude or a Bach fugue and the harmonic structure of that, and the ear training, where we’d have to sing and do solfeggio. That’s all helped with memorizing tunes. But nobody’s actually…
You haven’t gotten to jazz classes yet?
